question: In the fall of \(1996,\) a total of \(800\) students participated in an annual school clean-up day. The organizers of the event expect that in each of the years \(1997,\) \(1998,\) and \(1999,\) participation will increase by \(50\%\) over the previous year. The number of participants the organizers expect in the fall of \(1999\) is
solution:
A \(50\%\) increase adds half of the previous year's total. Each new total becomes the starting amount for the following year's increase. There are three increases:
\[
\begin{aligned}
1997:&\quad 800+400=1200,\\
1998:&\quad 1200+600=1800,\\
1999:&\quad 1800+900=2700.
\end{aligned}
\]
The organizers expect \(2700\) participants in the fall of \(1999\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
